tldr: Scored against our full 25-criteria rubric, Intercom out-scores Crisp on more than half the individual criteria — but Crisp is still the sharper pick on price, and neither vendor's AI-resolution claims survive independent scrutiny.

Crisp prices per workspace ($45-$295/mo bundling seats and AI credits); Intercom prices per seat ($29+/seat/mo) plus a separate $0.99-per-resolution AI fee — very different billing shapes for very different budgets.

Both ship a genuine AI agent (Crisp's 'Hugo', Intercom's 'Fin'), but neither vendor's self-reported resolution rate holds up: Crisp claims 50-60% automated resolution and Intercom claims 70-76%, while independent review data on both skews well below those numbers, especially outside well-documented FAQs.

Intercom edges out Crisp on native channels (adds real Phone/voice; Crisp needs an Aircall/KrispCall add-on), CRM sync, automation-platform integrations, and analytics depth — Crisp is close but not ahead on any of these.

Crisp's own Shopify/WooCommerce integration is genuinely strong (a native 'Get Order Details' tool for live tracking status), just a notch behind Intercom's, which Intercom itself built rather than licensed from a partner.

Pick Crisp if you want one affordable inbox for chat, WhatsApp, and social without enterprise pricing; pick Intercom if you want the more broadly capable, better-documented platform and can absorb per-seat-plus-per-resolution costs.

featureMatrix.toolB: Not independently tracked at comparable volume

verdict: Run the seat math first, because it's the clearest signal here: Crisp's $45/mo Mini plan works out to roughly $11/seat for a 4-person team, while Intercom's cheapest tier is a flat $29/seat no matter how many people you add — for a small team, Crisp is doing an entire inbox, WhatsApp, and social bundle for less than the cost of one single Intercom seat. What that price gap buys is real, though: scored against our full 25-criteria rubric, Intercom comes out ahead on native channel count, CRM sync, automation-platform integrations, and analytics depth, and its Shopify integration is Intercom's own build rather than a partner app. Neither one should be taken at its word on AI resolution, though — Crisp claims 50-60% automated resolution and Intercom claims 70-76%, and independent review data on both tools tells a noticeably less flattering story once you get past well-documented FAQ-style questions, which is why we scored AI resolution accuracy conservatively for both (2/5 and 3/5) rather than accepting either vendor's number at face value. The number that should actually worry you about Crisp isn't the AI, though — it's the 1.9/5 Trustpilot score, which reflects a real, specific pattern of billing and cancellation friction that Crisp's stronger G2/Capterra ratings don't surface, because those reviewers are rating day-to-day usability, not what happens when they try to leave. My honest read: if your support volume is mostly chat and messaging, budget is tight, and you're disciplined about reading cancellation terms before you sign, start with Crisp. If you want the more capable, more thoroughly-integrated platform across the board and can absorb Intercom's per-resolution costs, pay the premium for Intercom instead.
